transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Let's get our 15:00 disposition huddle started. We've got 120 returned servo drives from the customer to assess for possible remanufacture. I'll go through the standing checklist — Quality, Environmental Health and Safety, and Remanufacturing, in turn — for your go-or-no-go updates before I make the disposition decision and sign the work order. Let's start with Quality — what are your current findings on these returned drives?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: My serial-number reconciliation is complete: exactly 96 of the 120 returned drives have complete service histories and are eligible for remanufacture. The other 24 lack traceability and must remain quarantined. However, I should note that the reconciliation report is still in the quality review queue and has not yet reached Elena's release packet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: My battery-screening inspection found swollen lithium backup cells in exactly 18 of the returned drives. Those cells require a certified isolation procedure lasting exactly 2 hours before any remanufacturing work. My inspection worksheet is awaiting attachment to the EHS case.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thanks, Marta. Here's my Remanufacturing update for the checklist. I've completed my cell-capacity assessment: my remanufacturing cell can process the 96 traceable drives in exactly 16 hours once the battery isolation is complete. I've reserved that 16-hour work period on the cell board. However, I have not yet entered it in the production schedule. So from a Remanufacturing standpoint, we're ready capacity-wise, conditional on the battery isolation being completed and on the production schedule entry being finalized. I'm a no-go on final production schedule entry, but the cell capacity itself is confirmed for the 96 eligible units.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: 96 eligible drives are authorized for remanufacture only after: (1) Quality's serial-number reconciliation report is finalized and reaches Elena's release packet, (2) EHS completes the 2-hour certified battery isolation procedure on the 18 affected drives, and (3) Remanufacturing finalizes the production schedule entry for the 16-hour work period.
24 drives lacking serial traceability remain quarantined and are not eligible for remanufacture.
